title: Markdown Parser
description: Build a markdown-to-HTML parser with tokenizer, AST builder, and extensible renderer.

steps.title: Implement inline tokenizer
steps.description: Build a tokenizer that parses inline markdown syntax: bold (`**text**`), italic (`*text*`), inline code (`` `code` ``), and links (`[text](url)`). Print the list of tokens with their types and content in order.
hints: Process the input character by character, matching patterns with regex or state machine
Each token should have a {type, content} structure; links also need a url property
Handle escaped characters like \* by consuming the escape and treating the next char as literal

verification.successMessage: Tokenizer extracts bold, italic, code, and link tokens correctly
verification.failureMessage: Output missing one or more inline token types

steps.title: Build block-level parser
steps.description: Implement detection of block-level elements: headings (`# ` through `###### `), paragraphs, fenced code blocks (```` ``` ````), and horizontal rules (`---` or `***`). Print each detected block with its type and content.
hints: Split input by double newlines to get rough block boundaries, then classify each block
Heading level is determined by counting leading # characters
Fenced code blocks span multiple lines and may have a language identifier after the opening ```

verification.successMessage: Block parser correctly identifies headings, code blocks, and paragraphs

steps.title: Create AST from tokens
steps.description: Combine inline and block parsing to build an Abstract Syntax Tree. Each block node contains its children (inline tokens). Print the AST as formatted JSON showing the recursive structure.
hints: Block nodes become parent nodes with a children array holding inline token nodes
A paragraph node contains bold/italic/code children as sub-nodes in order
Use indentation in the JSON printout to visualize depth of nesting

verification.successMessage: AST prints as valid JSON with nested type and children structure
verification.failureMessage: AST output missing JSON structure or child relationships

steps.title: Implement HTML renderer
steps.description:
Walk the AST and generate HTML output. Bold becomes ``, italic becomes ``, code becomes ``, headings become `

`-`

`, paragraphs become `

`. Print the rendered HTML string.
hints: Match each node type to its corresponding HTML tag using a map or switch statement
Recursively render children before wrapping in the parent tag
Fenced code blocks should use <pre><code> with optional language class

verification.successMessage: HTML renderer produces correct markup for all element types

steps.title: Add nested block support
steps.description: Implement parsing for blockquotes (`> `) and nested lists (unordered `- ` and ordered `1. `). Support nesting up to 3 levels deep. Print the AST showing nested structure and the HTML output.
hints: Track the current nesting level by counting leading > or list indentation
Each nested level creates a child blockquote or list_item node inside the parent
For lists, alternate between ul and ol based on the list item marker type

verification.successMessage: Nested blocks parse and render as blockquotes and lists correctly
verification.failureMessage: Output missing blockquote or list elements

steps.title: Implement custom extension
steps.description: Create a plugin system that allows registering custom syntax extensions. Implement strikethrough (`~~text~~`) as an example extension that renders to `<del>`. Print the extended markdown output showing the new syntax working.
hints: Define an extension as an object with {name, match, render} properties
The tokenizer should check registered extensions after built-in patterns
Extensions register a regex pattern and a render function that returns an AST node

verification.successMessage: Custom extension renders strikethrough as <del> using the plugin system
verification.failureMessage: Extended output does not show strikethrough rendering

steps.title: Build a table parser
steps.description: Implement pipe-table syntax parsing: `| col1 | col2 |` with header separator `|---|---|`. Output an HTML `<table>` with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, and `<td>` elements. Print both the parsed table AST and the HTML output.
hints: Split the table into rows by newline, then split each row by | delimiter
The second row contains the alignment separator; cells with :--- are left-align, :--: center, ---: right
Inline markdown inside table cells should still be parsed by the inline tokenizer

verification.successMessage: Table parser generates proper HTML table structure
verification.failureMessage: HTML table output missing <table>, <tr>, or <td> tags
